description: Asymmetric mountain terrain with central valley. Two bases connected by ridgelines with passes. Mountains create LOS barriers and elevation advantages.

blue_base.description: Blue team spawn point. Safe territory, no contest expected in early game.

blue_near.description: Adjacent to Blue base. Easy early capture, minimal strategic decision required.

mountain_node_west.description: Elevated position on western mountain mass. Requires committing forces away from center corridor. Holding it extends defensive perimeter but overextends supply lines.
mountain_node_west.strategic_role: Optional territorial control. Losing it temporarily is strategically acceptable — fighting there distributes forces and respawn mechanics allow recapture.

center.description: Central valley between mountain masses. Both teams' natural advance routes converge here. First major contact point. Capture spawns reinforcements at the geographic midpoint.
center.strategic_role: Force multiplication hub. Capturing center creates a forward spawn that accelerates territorial expansion in both directions.

mountain_node_east.description: Elevated position on eastern mountain mass, deep in Red territory. Capturing requires pushing past center into enemy space.
mountain_node_east.strategic_role: Forward staging point. Rendezvous target — send NPC mechs via waypoint while tmech pushes ahead. Arriving first means protection from converging allies, and capture spawns additional mechs at this forward position.

red_near.description: Adjacent to Red base. Deep enemy territory. Capturing signals total map control.
red_near.strategic_role: Late-game objective. Only targeted once center and mountain nodes are secured.

red_base.description: Red team spawn point. Deepest enemy territory.
red_base.strategic_role: Final objective or ignored — game often decided before reaching this point.

convergence.definition: Geographic point where both teams' natural advance routes meet. First major decision point.
convergence.cognitive_demand: Assess band (2-8s). Quick evaluation: contest, capture, or bypass. Against passive AI, becomes Command band — capture and immediately pivot to next objective.
convergence.key_mechanic: Capture spawns reinforcements at geographic midpoint, enabling force projection in all directions.

commitment.definition: Position that requires dedicating forces away from the main axis of advance. Holding costs attention and units.
commitment.cognitive_demand: Sustained band (30s+) for the strategic calculus of whether to commit. L3-L4 reasoning: is holding this node worth the force distribution? Can I accept temporary loss because respawn mechanics favor recapture?
commitment.key_mechanic: Elevation provides LOS advantage. Capture spawns mechs at an elevated position. But committing forces here means fewer at center or on the main push.

recovery.definition: Safe territory near own base. Low cognitive demand, minimal decision-making.
recovery.cognitive_demand: Search/Glance band (<1s). No real decision — capture and move on.
recovery.key_mechanic: Respawn point. Force regeneration. Buffer against deep enemy penetration.

information.definition: Deep enemy territory where presence reveals opponent's base-level behavior and defensive posture.
information.cognitive_demand: Orient band (1-2s). Gathering intelligence about enemy state rather than making complex tactical decisions.
information.key_mechanic: Reaching this zone signals overwhelming advantage. The decision to push here vs. consolidate is the diagnostic signal.

central_valley.description: Low-ground corridor connecting Blue and Red territories through center node. Natural advance route for both teams.
central_valley.cognitive_role: Path of least resistance. Models may predict players use this exclusively, missing the mountain flanking options.

western_ridge.description: Mountain mass on western side of map. Node 4 sits on this elevation. Ridge creates LOS barrier between western approach and central valley.
western_ridge.cognitive_role: Commitment zone. Going here means not going center. The decision to split forces reveals L3+ strategic reasoning.

eastern_ridge.description: Mountain mass on eastern side. Node 2 sits here, deeper into Red territory than Node 4 is from Blue.
eastern_ridge.cognitive_role: Forward projection zone. Sending forces here while pushing center reveals parallel strategic thinking — waypoint NPCs to rendezvous while tmech advances.

perimeter_lowground.description: Low terrain around the outer edges of the mountain masses. Passable but exposed.
perimeter_lowground.cognitive_role: DIAGNOSTIC TRAP: Models may predict flanking via perimeter. In practice, the terrain doesn't reward this — the nodes are on the mountains, not around them. Predicting perimeter flanking reveals the model is reasoning from generic RTS heuristics rather than from this specific topology.

game_mechanics.capture: Only tmech (fastest, lightest unit) can capture nodes. Park near dome for 10s.
game_mechanics.spawn: Capturing a node spawns additional squad mechs AT that node. They respawn there when destroyed.
game_mechanics.respawn: Destroyed mechs respawn at their team's nearest captured node after 5 seconds.
game_mechanics.waypoints: Player can set waypoints via radar overlay (M key). RMB assigns waypoint, round-robin NPC assignment.
game_mechanics.tab_switch: Player can instantly switch between mechs after death or at any time.
game_mechanics.radar: M key toggles radar overlay showing all unit positions across terrain.
game_mechanics.los: Line of sight constrained by terrain heightmap. Mountains block visibility.
game_mechanics.asymmetry: Red is fast/fragile/short-range (rush playstyle). Blue is slow/durable/long-range (hold and siege).
